entries.name: Caribou (reindeer)
entries.migrates: between summer tundra calving grounds and winter taiga, herds of thousands

breeding.season: late summer rut, spring calving on the tundra

behaviour: both sexes grow antlers; bulls each autumn, cows in early summer
migrates along traditional routes between calving and wintering grounds
craters through snow with foot crescents to reach lichen
sounds: clacking of tendons at the ankles

voxel_model.pattern: pale neck mane and cream rump patch

entries.notes: The engine of the Arctic: calving aggregations on the tundra each June, then the long walk south. Tame reindeer are a real domestic form; the two names are the same animal.

entries.name: Muskox
behaviour: adults form a defensive ring, horns outward, around calves against wolves
stands and fights rather than flees
shaggy skirt hangs to the knees; guard hair tips pale

voxel_model.pattern: long shaggy guard hair, pale tips

entries.notes: A living ice-age survivor from the mammoth steppe, reintroduced across its former range. Qiviut (its down) is among the warmest natural fibres.

entries.name: Arctic fox
behaviour: full white winter coat, grey-brown in summer
trails polar bears to scavenge seal kills
caches food in burrows and frozen ground

voxel_model.pattern: seasonal white morph (winter), grey-brown (summer)

entries.notes: The tundra's classic scavenger-predator; watch for it at a polar bear kill. Winter-white and summer-brown morphs of the same fox.

entries.name: Arctic hare
behaviour: pure white winter coat; grey-brown in summer
stands on hind legs to scan over the sedge
furred young born in an open form above ground
entries.notes: Hares gather in loose groups of dozens on open ground in winter; the still-white form is invisible against old snow.

entries.name: Polar bear
entries.migrates: follows the sea-ice edge seasonally onto the tundra coast

breeding.season: spring births in coastal snow dens

behaviour: stalks seals at breathing holes in the sea ice
the strongest sense of smell of any bear, kilometres away
superb swimmer; ocean crossings of 60 km+
entries.notes: Top predator of the frozen coast; the spring tundra shore is its denning country. gestation_days includes delayed implantation.

entries.name: Arctic wolf
behaviour: all-white coat; pack coordinates ring hunts of muskoxen
loose track of caribou migrations rather than fixed territory
caches meat at rendezvous sites for pups
entries.notes: The purest-white subspecies; hunts the muskox ring only when caribou are scarce. White-on-white is the whole camouflage.

entries.name: Wolverine
entries.migrates: nomadic; home ranges of hundreds of square kilometres
behaviour: relentless pursuit predator across deep snow
crushes and caches frozen carrion; nothing on the tundra is wasted
notoriously bold at camp food stores and traplines

voxel_model.pattern: pale lateral mask stripe from shoulder to hip

entries.notes: One animal walks a home range the size of a county; it will find your field cache and eat it. Delayed implantation stretches breeding across two seasons.

entries.name: Brown lemming
entries.migrates: mass movements in boom years ('lemming runs')
behaviour: four-year population cycles; in boom years densities of thousands per hectare
winters in the subnivean space under the snow, still feeding
aggressively territorial year-round

voxel_model.pattern: dark dorsal band, pale flanks

entries.notes: The tundra's pulse: every predator on this list starves when the lemming cycle troughs. One model that eats, one model that runs, and the whole biome turns over.

entries.name: Collared lemming
behaviour: the only rodent that turns completely white in winter
grows oversized two-pronged claws in winter for digging through snow
caches willow and sedge in winter burrows

voxel_model.pattern: white winter morph with grey dorsal stripe

entries.notes: The High Arctic lemming; swapped claws and snow-digging are a lovely couple of frames for a winter state.

entries.name: Arctic ground squirrel

breeding.season: spring, in the days after hibernation ends

behaviour: hibernates seven to eight months; core body temperature drops below 0 °C, the coldest known of any hibernating mammal
two alarm calls: a whistle for raptors, a three-note chatter for ground predators
digs one-metre burrows above the permafrost line

voxel_model.pattern: lightly spotted back, white eye ring

entries.notes: Champion hibernator; females wake already pregnant in a below-freezing burrow. A siksik colony enlivens any dry ridge.

entries.name: Ermine (stoat)

breeding.season: midsummer mating, young born the following spring (delayed implantation)

behaviour: turns pure white in winter with a black-tipped tail
kills prey several times its own size with a bite behind the skull
hunts along snow tunnels, rodent burrows and underbrush

voxel_model.pattern: black-tipped tail, white winter coat

entries.notes: Long fuse of a predator; the black tail tip against the snow is the whole field mark. gestation_days is null: delayed implantation stretches mating to birth across two summers.

entries.name: Moose
behaviour: bulls grow broad palmate antlers up to 1.5 m across
wades into lakes and rivers to pull up water plants in summer
crescent craters where it paws through snow for forage
entries.notes: The world's largest deer; a treeline animal that strays well onto the open tundra in summer.

entries.name: Brown bear

breeding.season: summer mating, winter births in dens (delayed implantation)

behaviour: rips open ground squirrel burrows on the tundra
flips rocks and logs for grubs; strips salmon from tundra rivers
bulks up for hibernation in autumn hyperphagia
entries.notes: Far from the treeline it favours lemming nests and squirrel burrows over big game; least-risk rule: never corner one. gestation_days includes delayed implantation.

entries.name: Canada lynx
behaviour: ear tips carry long black tufts
oversized paws act as snowshoes in powder
population cycle locked to the snowshoe hare, about ten years

voxel_model.pattern: grey-brown with pale ruff; black ear tufts

entries.notes: A treeline and open-woodland cat; the black ear tufts and stub tail give it away at range.

entries.name: Ringed seal

breeding.season: births on the sea ice in spring

behaviour: scratches out snow lairs on the ice surface over breeding holes
keeps breathing holes open with its clawed foreflippers
pups are nursed in hidden lairs for four to six weeks

voxel_model.pattern: silver rings on the flanks (the name)

entries.notes: The polar bear's bread and butter; most of the frozen coast's calories pass through this animal. gestation_days is null: delayed implantation, up to eleven months total.

entries.name: Snowy owl
entries.migrates: nomadic; follows the lemming cycles over enormous ranges

breeding.season: late spring, timed to lemming booms

behaviour: males nearly pure white; females and juveniles barred brown
in boom lemming years the tundra is full of nesting pairs; in crash years most adults do not breed
sits on low rises and catches rodents by day in continuous daylight

voxel_model.pattern: male mostly white; female barred

entries.notes: The ghost of the tundra; a nomad that condenses out of nowhere in lemming years. gestation_days is incubation time.

entries.name: Rock ptarmigan
behaviour: white winter plumage with a black tail; mottled grey-brown in summer
scrapes a nest cup directly on the dry tundra
male gives harsh cackling calls from low rock outcrops

voxel_model.pattern: white winter plumage, black tail

entries.notes: The ptarmigan of the true Arctic: the rock-solid staple prey of the gyrfalcon. gestation_days is incubation time.

entries.name: Willow ptarmigan
behaviour: the lowland ptarmigan; more shrubby ground than rocks
male sings a resonant 'go-back, go-back' at dawn
winter flocks often of a dozen or more

voxel_model.pattern: white winter plumage, rusty-barred head

entries.notes: The game bird most people meet in the north; common in willow thicket and on the tundra edge. gestation_days is incubation time.

entries.name: Gyrfalcon
behaviour: the largest living falcon; white, grey and dark morphs
stoops on ptarmigan at well over 150 km/h
year-round resident of the tundra coast

voxel_model.pattern: white to grey to dark morph, barred

entries.notes: Falconry's most prized bird; the white morph of the high Arctic. gestation_days is incubation time; dives are far faster than its level cruise.

entries.name: Snow goose
entries.migrates: breeds in dense Arctic colonies; winters in the United States and Mexico

breeding.season: summer; an intensely short Arctic breeding window

behaviour: breeds in vast monochrome colonies, mostly white
grubs up the whole sedge sward with chisel-like bills
pairs for life; family groups stay together on migration

voxel_model.pattern: white body, black wingtips

entries.notes: Vast white flocks on migration; a hunter's waterfowl and a deafening roost at dawn. gestation_days is incubation time.

entries.name: Tundra swan
entries.migrates: breeds on the Arctic coast; winters on mid-latitude estuaries
behaviour: the largest North American waterfowl next to the trumpeter
migrates in V-formations with steady powerful beats
bugling calls carry for kilometres over open ground
entries.notes: Heavier on the wing than expected; a black-billed swan that yips like a bugle. gestation_days is incubation time.

entries.name: Barnacle goose
entries.migrates: breeds on Greenland, Svalbard and Arctic Russia; winters on west European coasts
behaviour: black neck and breast with a white face mask
nests on sheer cliff ledges beyond fox reach
nonstop migration flights of several weeks

voxel_model.pattern: black neck and barred back

entries.notes: Ancient name confusion: barnacles were once thought to hatch into these geese. gestation_days is incubation time.

entries.name: Arctic tern
entries.migrates: pole to pole every year — the longest migration on Earth, roughly 40,000 km each way
behaviour: grey back, blood-red bill and legs, black cap in summer
dive-bombs any head near the nest, drawing blood with its beak
sees more daylight in a year than any other creature

voxel_model.pattern: black cap, forked tail streamers

entries.notes: The world champion of migration; colony birds will mob the player who wanders too close. gestation_days is incubation time.

entries.name: Parasitic jaeger
entries.migrates: breeds on the Arctic coast; winters at sea worldwide
behaviour: terrorises terns and gulls in high-speed chases until they drop their catch
kleptoparasite first, hunter second; also takes eggs and lemmings
long central tail streamers in breeding adults

voxel_model.pattern: brown to pale morph, white flash at rump

entries.notes: The pirate of the tundra coast; watch it rob a tern mid-air. gestation_days is incubation time.

entries.name: Rough-legged buzzard
entries.migrates: breeds on the open tundra; winters on southern plains and steppes

breeding.season: late spring, timed to lemming abundance

behaviour: feathered tarsi down to the toes for cold perching
hovers facing into the wind over open ground, scanning for rodents
dark and pale morphs coexist in the same landscape

voxel_model.pattern: dark belly band and carpal patches

entries.notes: A hover over nowhere with the patience of winter; second only to the owl as a lemming hunter. gestation_days is incubation time.

entries.name: Common raven
behaviour: problem-solver: pulls fishing line, unzips packs, drops shellfish on rock
loyal mated pairs and family groups
follows wolves, bears and hunters to carrion like a camp dog

voxel_model.pattern: wedge-shaped tail, shaggy throat hackles

entries.notes: The tundra's camp follower; watches wolves and hunters alike and remembers every cache. gestation_days is incubation time.

entries.name: Snow bunting
entries.migrates: breeds on the Arctic and alpine tundra; winters on open temperate ground
behaviour: pure white winter plumage; black-and-tan in breeding dress
nests in rock crevices and building cracks
one of the very few passerines of the high Arctic

voxel_model.pattern: white with black wings and tail tips

entries.notes: A cheerful little tune in an empty white landscape. gestation_days is incubation time.

entries.name: Lapland longspur
entries.migrates: breeds across the Arctic tundra; winters on temperate grasslands and stubble
behaviour: the most abundant songbird of the tundra
male sings a bubbling, descending warble in flight
winters in huge flocks on weedy fields

voxel_model.pattern: black face with rust nape in summer

entries.notes: Listen for this one before you see it; the tundra's background musician. gestation_days is incubation time.

entries.name: Red phalarope
entries.migrates: breeds on Arctic tundra pools; winters on open tropical oceans
behaviour: role reversal: bright female courts and leaves; duller male incubates
spins on the water to raise a tiny vortex and suck in prey
winters far out at sea, far from any land

voxel_model.pattern: chestnut breeding plumage, dark cap

entries.notes: A polyandrous wader that thinks upside-down: spin-feeding like a whirlpool. gestation_days is incubation time.

entries.name: Ivory gull
entries.migrates: high-Arctic wanderer; follows the drift ice and polar bears
behaviour: pure porcelain white with a black beak tip
trails polar bears to pick seal carcasses clean
among the fastest-declining Arctic birds as sea ice retreats

voxel_model.pattern: near-total white, dark bill tip

entries.notes: A ghost-white gull that exists off bear kills and moving ice; near-threatened. gestation_days is incubation time.

entries.name: Arctic char
entries.migrates: anadromous and resident forms; runs up tundra rivers to spawn

breeding.season: autumn; eggs over winter in gravel redds

behaviour: the northernmost freshwater fish on Earth
forked tail, light spots on dark flanks
sea-run fish feed in the Arctic Ocean and return to river gravel

voxel_model.pattern: orange-red belly in spawning dress, pale spots

entries.notes: The landlocked tundra lakes' prize fish and the coastal summer run's bonanza. gestation_days is null for a fish; eggs incubate through the winter.

entries.name: Arctic mosquito

breeding.season: hatches en masse on the spring thaw

behaviour: emerges in uncountable clouds the moment melt pools form
males drink nectar only; females need a blood meal to lay
the constant drone around any warm-blooded animal on a July afternoon
entries.notes: The tundra's tax on summer: no model needed at distance, but the drone and the itch are its signature.

entries.name: Arctic bumblebee

breeding.season: summer; only queens survive the winter

behaviour: one of the bees that ranges into the high Arctic
shiver-warms its flight muscles to fly near 0 °C
buzz-pollinates mountain avens and other tundra blooms

voxel_model.pattern: banded yellow, black and white

entries.notes: Proof the tundra blooms can be worked by insects: a furry wasp of the midnight sun.

entries.name: Arctic woolly bear moth

breeding.season: brief June flight; females are flightless

behaviour: caterpillar development stretches over up to seven Arctic summers
basks on rocks to warm; survives -70 °C in supercooled winter diapause
adult moths live only weeks, in June

voxel_model.pattern: dense banded fuzz, rust and black

entries.player: not interactable; a slow crawling fuzzball
entries.notes: The slowest animal on this list: a caterpillar that may have started feeding seven years ago. An extreme marvel for the curious player.

entries.name: Arctic wolf spider

breeding.season: summer; female carries the egg sac under her abdomen

behaviour: active on snow and in full sun at 0 °C
hunts entirely by sprint; spins no web
densest spider on the tundra; a key invertebrate predator
entries.notes: The tundra's house centipede of the food web: nearly everything eats it, and it eats nearly everything smaller.
